requirement:
Structural hashes use SHA-256 over the unambiguous structural encoding and
whitespace-separated words under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`.
The fingerprint scheme identifies these rules and their version under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.language_provider.fingerprint_scheme`.

Ordinary comments are excluded. Docstrings are source expressions and
participate in hashes along with the definition's other expressions.
rationale:
The reviewed tests cover each obligation in `requirements.sdk.sources.python.fingerprints`. I did not read the implementation. I checked the tests against the requirement text only.

- **Comments excluded.** In `src/outline/tests.rs#fn[comments_are_excluded_from_hashes_in_every_other_profile]`, the Python case changes a leading comment and a trailing comment, and also removes both. The hash of `def[f]` is unchanged in every variant. Changing the non-comment word (`x` to `y`) changes the hash. In `tests/outline_content.rs#fn[bundled_fingerprints_exclude_comments_and_preserve_word_boundaries]`, a Python comment edit combined with a whitespace edit leaves the fingerprint equal.
- **Whitespace-separated words, with word boundaries kept.** The same test changes `"two words"` to `"two   words"`, which keeps the hash. Changing it to `"twowords"` changes the hash, so `ab cd` and `abcd` differ.
- **Docstrings participate.** The same test builds a Python docstring `"""two words"""` and checks both directions:
  - Widening the whitespace inside it leaves the fingerprint equal.
  - Changing the words to `changed words` changes the fingerprint.

  So the docstring counts as a source expression in the hash, and it is hashed by words.
- **SHA-256 digest.** The Python test asserts the fingerprint value is 64 hex characters. The SHA-256 digest itself is pinned by the known-vector test in `src/outline/tests.rs#fn[hashes_include_grammar_kinds_nesting_and_sha256_digests]`. That test uses the shared `Encoder` in `outline/hash.rs`, which is the same hasher the Python profile goes through. I did not read `outline/hash.rs` beyond the search snippet, so I did not confirm the Python path reaches that `Encoder`.
- **Fingerprint scheme.** `tests/outline_content.rs#fn[bundled_languages_claim_extensions_and_supply_the_same_public_outline]` asserts `languages::Python.fingerprint_scheme()` is `"python-structural-v1"`. It also asserts that `OutlineContent::fingerprint_scheme()` of the loaded content equals the language's scheme, which covers "loaded contents retain the scheme".
- **Python attachments in the hash.** `src/outline/tests.rs#fn[python_decorators_attach_to_the_decorated_definition_for_hashing]` shows that decorator edits, and removing the decorator, change the definition's structural hash. Whitespace and blank-line changes do not. A method's decorator changes its class's structural hash but not its identity hash. This supports the "definition's other expressions" part.

No obligation in the subject text lacks a test that asserts its outcome. No acknowledgments (`{fixme}`) apply or are needed.

text: :::{req} fingerprints
Structural hashes use SHA-256 over the unambiguous structural encoding and
whitespace-separated words under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`.
The fingerprint scheme identifies these rules and their version under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.language_provider.fingerprint_scheme`.
Ordinary comments are excluded. Docstrings are source expressions and
participate in hashes along with the definition's other expressions.
:::{req} structural_hash
A node's structural hash MUST be the SHA-256 digest of an unambiguous encoding of
its outline-relevant structure, including siblings its profile attaches to it:
the kinds of its named grammar nodes and, in source order, its text pieces. A
text piece MUST be the text of a leaf token, or text inside a node that no child
token covers. Each text piece MUST be hashed as its ordered list of words, where
words are separated by whitespace, the whitespace itself, including leading and
trailing whitespace, is never hashed, and each word is encoded separately, so
`ab cd` and `abcd` differ. The same rule MUST apply in every language. Comments
MUST be excluded, except comment kinds the profile includes; the Rust profile MUST include doc comments. For an included comment, only its text and its
profile's comment group MUST be hashed, not its delimiter tokens such as `//`,
`///`, `//!`, `/*`, `*/`, or a leading `*`; the Rust profile's groups are inner
and outer doc comments. The words of consecutive included comments of one group
MUST be hashed as one ordered list, so reflowing them across more or fewer lines
or comments does not change the hash, while moving text between groups does. A `line`
node's hash MUST be computed by the same word rule over the line's text. A node's
identity hash MUST be computed the same way but MUST also exclude its outline
descendants and their attached siblings, so editing a descendant does not change
its ancestors' selectors.
:::{req} language_provider.fingerprint_scheme
Each language supplies the scheme identifying its structural-hash rules and
their version. A change to those rules uses a different scheme; an update
preserving the calculation can retain the scheme. Loaded contents retain the
scheme used to compute their hashes.
```rust,ignore
pub trait OutlineLang: Clone + Send + Sync {
/// Identify the structural-hash rules and their version.
fn fingerprint_scheme(&self) -> &str;
impl OutlineContent {
/// The selected item's structural digest from this snapshot.
pub fn structural_hash(&self) -> &str;
/// The retained scheme identifying its hashing rules and version.
pub fn fingerprint_scheme(&self) -> &str;
